She reported it. It got patched. Crypto was saved.
Her reward? Just $55K.
But this isn’t even her first time.
She also exposed a16z leaking AWS keys, database credentials, and PII—sitting in inspect element.
That hack could’ve compromised one of the biggest VCs in crypto.
Her reward? $0.
Then, she discovered a way to hijack someone’s Arc browser without them even visiting a website — letting attackers execute arbitrary JavaScript on any page.
That time, she got $2K.
$57K total for stopping multiple disasters.
Some people break crypto. Xyzeva keeps saving it.

RT Eric Wall | BIP-420 🐱
If you want to understand what happens to funds after they’re stolen by North Korea/Lazarus Group, the Chainalysis 2022 report is great
Step 1: Swap any ERC20s (like stETH) into ETH 
Step 2: Swap any ETH into BTC 
Step 3: Cash out BTC to cash (Chinese Renminbi) using Asian exchanges 
This process can take years. They are in no hurry. 
In 2022, it was noted how North Korea was still sitting on $55 worth of funds from hacks that happened six years earlier (2016).
